cases.original_forecast: More added CO2 is accommodated by dissolved inorganic-carbon species than an equal N2 dose, changing the pressure increment.

original_criteria_review.criterion: Compare gas-phase fractions of the added material, not pressure alone.
original_criteria_review.reason: Subtract each arm’s own trapped-air baseline: the added N2 remains an ideal inert carrier while part of the equal CO2 dose enters owned aqueous carbon.

original_criteria_review.criterion: The CO2 vessel should store more of the dose in the liquid under these conditions.
original_criteria_review.reason: The actual CO2 arm stores more of its dose in liquid. This supports the original qualitative comparison within the ideal-carrier domain; quantitative real N2 dissolution is not implemented or certified.

cases.qualification: Historical ideal-carrier/aqueous-carbonate model. No current-production, empirical solubility, general nonideal-gas, quantitative N2 uptake or reaction-energy certification.

cases.original_forecast: Warming normally favours CO2 release into the gas phase. Pressure also changes directly with temperature, so phase inventories are needed to separate the effects.

original_criteria_review.criterion: Compare dissolved-carbon fractions, not just the raw pressure difference.
original_criteria_review.reason: Compare the actual dissolved-carbon fractions at both recorded temperatures and each finite trapped-air baseline; the warm arm retains a smaller fraction.

original_criteria_review.criterion: Check whether the runtime uses temperature-dependent partition data; fixed-Henry behaviour is a model limitation.
original_criteria_review.reason: The actual pinned WATEQ CO2 phase has a five-coefficient temperature relation and nonzero dissolution enthalpy. This is temperature-dependent native partitioning, not fixed-Henry or pressure-only inference; no empirical calibration is earned.

cases.qualification: Historical ideal-carrier/aqueous-carbonate model. No current-production, empirical solubility, general nonideal-gas, quantitative N2 uptake or reaction-energy certification.

cases.original_forecast: Base captures the CO2 dose as inorganic-carbon ions; acidification reverses that storage and moves carbon back toward molecular and gas-phase CO2.

original_criteria_review.criterion: Carbonate/bicarbonate decline after acidification while headspace CO2 increases.
original_criteria_review.reason: Owned bicarbonate/carbonate decrease after acidification while gas CO2 increases, at the actual recorded temperatures.

original_criteria_review.criterion: Total carbon is conserved across the capture–release cycle, apart from explicitly recorded initial air contributions.
original_criteria_review.reason: The original finite carbon dose closes against its trapped-air baseline, and acid addition closes independently for all represented atoms/charge. Carbon is redistributed rather than deleted or supplied externally.

cases.original_forecast: Adding inert gas to a fixed headspace increases total pressure without adding carbon. In an ideal mixture at fixed temperature, it does not directly multiply CO2 partial pressure.

original_criteria_review.criterion: Total pressure rises, but total carbon remains unchanged.
original_criteria_review.reason: Total pressure rises at fixed headspace while all owned carbon is conserved; the nitrogen addition closes independently.

original_criteria_review.criterion: Compare CO2 partial pressure and dissolved-carbon fraction before and after; account for thermal and nonideal corrections.
original_criteria_review.reason: Actual-temperature CO2 partial pressures and dissolved fractions are compared explicitly. Removing the recorded temperature ratio leaves a unit partial-pressure ratio at inventory resolution. The pinned phase’s ideal EOS domain is explicit; no nonideal gas correction is silently claimed.

additional_metrics.nonideal_correction_scope: The actual WATEQ CO2 phase lacks critical-parameter EOS entries and uses ideal gas behavior; inert N2 is an excluded-redox carrier. No real-gas correction or empirical fugacity claim. The original forecast is conditional on ideal mixing.
